p: The Lakeside branch is a good choice for families from across Essex and the edge of London, as getting there by car is so straightforward. The M25 and the Dartford Crossing are right on the doorstep, and Chafford Hundred station is within walking distance for anyone coming by train. Before you head in, have a look at the games available, as some are tailored towards younger kids while others are geared up for teenagers and adults.

The area around Lakeside has more going for it than most people realise. Chafford Gorges Nature Park, just next to the shopping area, is a network of old chalk quarries that have been turned into a wildlife haven, with lakes, cliffs and walking trails. It's a great place for a stroll and some fresh air after the excitement of your game, and the visitor centre has views across the gorges.

History fans should head to Tilbury Fort, a little further east along the Thames. Run by English Heritage, it's a superb star-shaped fort that has guarded the river approach to London for centuries. Kids love exploring the bastions and the moat. Coalhouse Fort at East Tilbury is another fascinating Victorian fort with riverside walks.

For a nature fix, RSPB Rainham Marshes is just over the boundary near Purfleet, with boardwalks across ancient marshland and lots of birdlife to spot. And if you just want to take it easy, the lake beside the shopping centre has a pleasant path around it for a wander and some views of the water. From the riverside at Grays or Purfleet you also get a cracking view of the Queen Elizabeth II Bridge, the huge cable-stayed crossing that carries southbound Dartford Crossing traffic high over the Thames.
